changes_made.explanation: Consolidated duplicate model entries, normalized naming conventions, simplified task categories, and refined output descriptions for clarity.
Removed redundant metric variants (e.g., 'BLEU score' → 'BLEU') and standardized naming to base metric forms.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted in the paper; LLMs are used only for text generation, not for post-generation assessment.

guideline: Annotators rank three generated texts based on closeness to input data (faithfulness) and fluency using four questions: closest text to data, farthest text from data, most fluent text, least fluent text.

Annotators rank three generated texts based on closeness to input data (faithfulness) and fluency using four questions: closest text to data, farthest text from data, most fluent text, least fluent text.

The annotators are then asked to answer the following four questions about the three texts: • Please, select the text which is the closest to the data shown. Consider both additions and omissions. • Please, select the text which is the farthest from the data shown. Consider both additions and omissions. • Please, select the text which is the most fluent. • Please, select the text which is the least fluent.
Annotators rank each of the three generated texts based on (i) closeness to the data (additions/omissions) and (ii) fluency, using the four questions above.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into a single clear statement and confirmed faithfulness/fluency as the evaluation criteria.

overall_notes: Extraction quality was generally good. The paper focuses on Knowledge Graph-to-Text generation for Russian, comparing fine-tuning, prompting, and RAG methods. All metadata was well-supported in the text with minor normalization needed for consistency.
